syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every discontinuity answers two questions: do the sides exist and agree, and does the value match? Agreement plus mismatch is removable (repairable by one value); finite disagreement is a jump (size = |RHL − LHL|); blow-up is a wall (odd splits, even unifies); no side limit is oscillatory. Rational functions triage by factorisation — cancelled roots are holes, surviving roots are walls.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Removable: lim exists, f(a) ≠ L or undefined ⟹ repair f(a) = L - Jump: LHL ≠ RHL, both finite; size = |RHL − LHL|

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Calling $|x|$ at 0 removable — it is a JUMP, because the one-sided limits are governed by different branches rather than one wrong value.  ·  Saying an infinite discontinuity 'has limit infinity' — infinity is not a value, so the real limit does not exist.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Calling $|x|$ at 0 removable — it is a JUMP, because the one-sided limits are governed by different branches rather than one wrong value.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The wall with a dot*** - assigning f(2) = 1/4 at a wall's foot changes nothing: walls live in the neighbourhood, dots live at the point.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Assuming a hole is harmless for differentiation — it blocks the derivative even though both one-sided limits agree.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Sides first, value second - the order of the tree is the order of the marks.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Classify the discontinuity of f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) for x ≠ 1 with f(1) = 3, and state the repair.** — **Sides:** (x²−1)/(x−1) = x + 1 for x ≠ 1 ⟹ LHL = **2**, RHL = **2** — sides exist and agree ⟹ limit L = 2. **Value:** f(1) = 3 ≠ 2.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find and classify all discontinuities of f(x) = (x + 1)/(x² − 5x + 6).** — **Factor:** (x − 2)(x − 3) ⟹ suspects {2, 3}; numerator at 2 is 3 ≠ 0, at 3 is 4 ≠ 0 ⟹ no cancellation, both are walls. **At x = 2:** denominator ≈ (x−2)(−1); x → 2⁺ ⟹ small negative ⟹ → **−∞**; x → 2⁻ ⟹ → **+∞** (splitting).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State the repair verdict explicitly: "removable, repair f(a) = L" or "non-removable".

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Two binary questions classify every discontinuity; the repair test separates point-sickness from neighbourhood-sickness.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Decision tree: sides exist and agree? No -> jump (finite unequal), infinite (blow-up, odd splits/even unifies), or oscillatory. Yes -> limit L exists; f(a) = L? Yes -> continuous; No -> removable, repair f(a) = L. Rational triage: cancelled roots are holes, surviving denominator roots are walls.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Removable breaks leave every limit intact; only continuity and value questions see them.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): For f(x) = x for x < 2, f(x) = 7 − 2x for x ≥ 2: classify the behaviour at x = 2 fully.** — **LHL:** lim_{x→2⁻} x = **2**. **RHL:** lim_{x→2⁺} (7 − 2x) = 7 − 4 = **3**. **Value:** f(2) = 3 (≥ owns the point).…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): For f(x) = (x³ − 1)/(x² − 1) for x ≠ 1 with f(1) = k: find k for continuity and classify what happens at x = −1.** — **Factor:** x³ − 1 = (x−1)(x² + x + 1); x² − 1 = (x−1)(x+1) ⟹ f(x) = (x² + x + 1)/(x + 1) for x ≠ 1.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to the Discontinuity Taxonomy This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to the types of discontinuity: the decision tree that sorts every break into removable, jump, infinite, or oscillatory in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **The two questions:** (1) do the one-sided limits exist and agree? (2) does f(a) match the merged limit? - **Removable:** sides agree (limit L exists) but f(a) is missing or ≠ L — hole or detached dot; **repairable** by f(a) = L. - **Jump:** sides exist, finite, **unequal** — vertical gap of size |RHL − LHL|; non-removable.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — The Taxonomy Is a Decision Tree, Not a List - Two binary questions — sides agree? value matches? — generate all four types. Computing in the right order (sides first, value second) makes classification mechanical: no agreement ⟹ jump/infinite/oscillatory by the sides' behaviour; agreement ⟹ removable or continuous by the value.…

Deep Conceptual — Where Each Type Lives in Mathematics - **Removable breaks are cancellation shadows:** 0/0 forms are shared roots wearing disguises; the limit sees through them, continuity does not.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — rational audit:** factor fully; cancelled roots ⟹ holes with limits; surviving roots ⟹ walls with side signs. - **Type B — piecewise seam:** LHL from the left branch, RHL from the right, f(a) from the owning branch; unanimous agreement ⟹ continuous.…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Any break is a jump":** jumps need finite *unequal* sides — compute before naming. **"f(a) defined ⟹ no discontinuity":** a wrong value is a removable break, not immunity.
